Five kinds of evidence

Technique · Labour · Law · Finance · Public story.

1 · Not genius vs theft

Investigate. Success ≠ originality. Reuse ≠ theft.

[Mina Edison] maintained a friendly relationship with the press, helped cultivate Edison’s public image as a genius …

(Robb 2024, 243)

Book review = a lead, not a verdict. Who builds the “genius” image in your case?

Thomas Edison with his tin-foil phonograph, Brady studio, Washington, c. 1878 · Levin C. Handy (Brady-Handy studio) · Public domain · Source

2 · Five cases

Light system · Phonograph · Cinema · Radio (counter) · Patent company.

Phonograph: strong Edison contribution. Radio: not an Edison invention claim.

Phonograph drawings, 29 November 1877 · Thomas A. Edison (drawing; Thomas Edison National Historical Park, National Park Service) · Public domain · Source

3 · The system can be the creative act

Wiring · generators · meters · sockets — the world around the object.

4 · Scale of participation

One eye at a peephole ≠ a room watching a screen.

5 · Standards can choke

Shared formats help industry — and can lock the gate.

6 · Two maps, not one

Who made it ≠ who gets the value. Keep the maps apart until you can say why they diverge.

Generate numerous ideas. It is dangerous to become fixated upon one or two ideas too early in the process.

(Norman 2013, 226)

Exercise 1 · Two maps

Save both maps in the portfolio index.

Exercise 2 · Change who owns it

Keep what it does. Change who owns it — and who pays to keep it.

Ownership model + cost of upkeep — feeds the bridge dossier.
